newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador's first Eurobond due for issue shortly.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador's first Eurobond due for issue shortly.

text.p: The general manager of Ecuador's Central Bank, Fidel Jaramillo, said Thursday that Chase Manhattan Bank is studying the conditions of the country's first Eurobond issue to be placed within weeks.
"Chase is currently analyzing the amount of demand, the orders from investors and the prices offered," Jaramillo told journalists.
Chase is lead managing the issue. The process of launching the bond was begun under former President Abdala Bucaram. His ouster by Congress in February led to a delay of the issue.
"It is a process which will conclude this or next week with the announcement of the placement, the amount, the price and the exact conditions," Jaramillo said.
Jaramillo's statements came after rumors Wednesday that the issue would be delayed again.

A source close to the deal in New York said the issue is now likely to be in two parts with a five-year fixed rate issue and a seven-year floating rate note. The fixed paper would come in around 475 basis points over Treasuries, syndicate sources said.

Initial speculation was that the bond would have a five-year maturity and that it would be priced around 350 basis points over similarly dated U.S. Treasuries. The amount would be between $300 million and $400 million.
Jaramillo said the first $300 million raised through the bond will be used to pay off a loan granted to Ecuador by Chase in December.
